headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: both docs-only agents can share sensitive context through files and outputs, while A’s broad egress and B’s shell/write access create unsafe default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can ingest browser/file content and use runtime-injected MCPs/hooks; B can read/write files and consume stdin/stdout, so a prompt-injection bridge exists if B’s outputs are copied into A or shared files. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from capabilities rather than observed behavior.
conditions: IF B writes attacker-controlled instructions into a file A later reads
IF the orchestrator copies B stdout into A prompts without filtering
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
Restrict A to allowlisted input paths
Review B outputs before forwarding to A

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches session history, project code, and provider auth data and has broad network egress; B touches configuration secrets and can read/write the filesystem. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from either agent into A’s outbound APIs or B’s local files, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default-like setups.
conditions: IF A and B share any filesystem containing secrets or session history
IF A forwards file contents to external APIs during normal operation
IF B reads files that A has written containing credentials
mitigations: Block A from sending raw file contents off-host

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A supports multiple instances and task-scoped isolation, while B supports multiple instances with local-development self-isolation and write access. Even without git writes, both can mutate overlapping files or project state if pointed at the same workspace, so write conflicts are plausible and not prevented by documented locking.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree
IF either agent writes configuration or notebook files the other also edits
mitigations: Use read-only mounts for one agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce tool-augmented outputs and B exposes agentic ask/stream endpoints plus shell execution. If B treats A’s generated content as authoritative, A’s mistakes can cascade into B’s downstream actions or generated writing. No verification boundary is documented, so the safer higher severity applies.
conditions: IF B consumes A outputs as prompts or facts without verification
IF B uses A-generated text to drive shell commands or API calls
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require citations for A outputs before B uses them
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff messages

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider authentication data and session history; B handles configuration secrets and course data. Both are docs-only and no residency or certification mismatch is documented, but the pair can mix sensitive classes with different retention expectations, so compliance risk exists through shared handling rather than a specific regulated-data breach.
conditions: IF regulated or customer secrets are placed into the shared workflow
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two environments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention for each agent separately
Store secrets in a dedicated vault
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
